A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LightRetriever research. Their complete main texts, Appendices A.1–A.8, equations, figures, and tables are readable and support reliable comparison despite the changed title.

before.justification: v3 reports original retrieval accuracy and timing experiments, architecture ablations, KL-loss comparisons, and index-compression experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results, including Tables 1–5 and 9–11 and the dimension/sparsity experiments in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The dense token-embedding cache, token-count sparse queries, full document encoder, and training components remain unchanged. Section 2.3 drops its auxiliary-loss reference, but Appendix A.4 retains the KL objective and identical with/without-KL results; this does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 20 English and three Chinese training datasets, 15 BeIR and eight CMTEB Retrieval evaluation datasets, and Bing-query/MSMARCO timing scenario. The added dataset-level discussion introduces no new coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding comparisons: Static Embedding, BM25, their combination, BGE-m3 variants, LLM2Vec, E5-Mistral, and full symmetric retrievers. The appendix comparisons also retain their methods.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, preprocessing, evaluation splits, and nDCG/recall metrics match. The speed experiment still uses 65,536 queries over one million passages, an A800 GPU, and batch size 256. No revised experimental setting is reported.

E4.justification: The architecture ablations, reversed-asymmetry failure observation, dense/sparse/hybrid comparison, dimension/sparsity sweep, and auxiliary-KL ablation are retained. Moving Table 4 beside Table 3 changes presentation, not the analyses performed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The annotated score differences remain performance gaps rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged. Section 3.2 adds a qualitative summary distinguishing strong performance on named general retrieval benchmarks from larger losses on FiQA and CmedQA, described as around five points. This adds a reported trend based on existing appendix results.

T1.justification: v3 Equations 3 and 4 are combined into v4 Equation 3 without changing their mathematics. The remaining loss definitions, attention mask, and sparse-aggregation reasoning are retained; equation renumbering introduces no theoretical revision.

C1.justification: The central contribution and claims remain lightweight query encoding, over 1000-fold encoding speedup, over tenfold retrieval throughput, and approximately 95% retained performance. Replacing the title's numerical speedup with 'Extremely Faster' does not withdraw the quantitative claims retained in the abstract.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly characterizes domain-specific performance losses as tolerable and suggests future task-specific adaptation. This adds a qualification to the generalization discussion. The mechanism explanations and Appendix A.1 limitation concerning non-LLM architectures remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The introduction removes v3's explicit statement that dense scores use cosine similarity while sparse scores use inner products. Section 2.3 also removes the KL-loss cross-reference, although Appendix A.4 retains its treatment. Hyperparameters, optimization pseudocode, hardware, and code/data access disclosures otherwise match.

R1.justification: v4 adds Craswell et al., 'Overview of the TREC 2019 Deep Learning Track,' as reference 16, cited alongside TRECCOVID in the new results discussion. Existing cited works and Appendix A.2's research positioning are retained; subsequent reference-number shifts are not additional changes.

P1.justification: Several introduction and performance-discussion paragraphs are rewritten, the title changes, and method explanations are shortened. These localized edits preserve the overall section order and appendix organization.

P2.justification: Tables 3 and 4 become adjacent displays on page 8, with explicit A1–A3 result labels and a defined '1L-Trans' abbreviation. Equation consolidation and text reflow adjust layout. Existing figures and remaining table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies the motivation and makes ablation settings and results easier to compare. However, it removes explicit cosine-scoring information and adds an imprecise 'around five points' summary: retained Tables 9 and 11 show Llama-8B losses of 8.3 on FiQA and 7.4 on CmedQA. These readability gains and losses of technical precision leave the net quality direction uncertain.
